headline: AI Guides Surgeon to Save Patient's Vision in Historic Brain Operation
meta_description: Surgeons at UCL Hospital used real-time AI assistance during brain surgery to remove a pituitary tumour threatening a patient's sight—a medical first.
summary_short: Rhys Hibbert, 48, became the first patient to benefit from live AI support during neurosurgery. The system helped surgeons navigate around critical nerves and blood vess…
body:
For the first time, artificial intelligence guided a neurosurgeon in real time during live brain surgery. Rhys Hibbert, 48, underwent the landmark procedure at University College London Hospital in August 2026 to remove a pituitary tumour that threatened to cause blindness.

During the operation, an AI system developed by UCL analysed the live surgical video feed and highlighted critical structures—nerves and blood vessels—that the surgeon needed to avoid. The technology provided moment-by-moment support, allowing the medical team to navigate one of the brain's most delicate regions with unprecedented precision.

The surgery addressed an urgent medical need: Hibbert's tumour was actively threatening his vision and could have led to permanent blindness without intervention. By combining human expertise with AI's ability to instantly recognise and flag vital anatomical structures, the team achieved what traditional surgery alone might not have accomplished as safely.
